# Environment Format Reference

Use these examples as patterns, not as universal templates. Inspect the project first and adapt to its real run commands.

## Simple Command

Use a single-line command when the project has one reliable startup entrypoint.

```toml
# THIS IS AUTOGENERATED. DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
version = 1
name = "desktop-app"

[setup]
script = ""

[[actions]]
name = "运行"
icon = "run"
command = "make run-gui"
```

## Subdirectory Frontend

Use a multiline literal string when changing directories before starting one process.

```toml
# THIS IS AUTOGENERATED. DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
version = 1
name = "web-app"

[setup]
script = ""

[[actions]]
name = "运行"
icon = "run"
command = '''
cd frontend
bun dev
'''
```

## Environment Files Are The Source Of Truth

Keep application configuration in the project's established ignored environment file. An environment action or wrapper should load and validate that file, not duplicate its values.

```dotenv
# .env.example: tracked key contract with placeholders only
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/app
APP_API_KEY=replace-with-local-key
PORT=8080
```

For a real local `.env`, preserve the user's existing values and confirm the file is ignored. Use the project's dotenv loader or a structured parser so credentials containing shell metacharacters are not evaluated as shell code. If the wrapper needs parsed values for dependency setup or health checks, emit only explicitly allowlisted runner-derived fields rather than exporting the entire dotenv map. A wrapper may report `DATABASE_URL is missing`, but it must not print the value.

If a runner creates a disposable PostgreSQL container, parse the local `DATABASE_URL` and use its host, port, user, password, and database for container setup. Do not repeat those values as literals in the wrapper.

## Multi-Process Frontend And Backend

For multi-process workflows, prefer a wrapper script and keep `environment.toml` to one absolute command. This is more stable in the Codex App terminal than pasting a large multiline shell program from TOML.

```toml
# THIS IS AUTOGENERATED. DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
version = 1
name = "full-stack-app"

[setup]
script = ""

[[actions]]
name = "运行"
icon = "run"
command = "/bin/bash /Users/me/projects/full-stack-app/.codex/environments/run-dev.sh"
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:$PATH"

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "${api_pid:-}" ]; then
    kill "$api_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

(
  cd backend
  make run-api
) &
api_pid=$!

until curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8084/healthz >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done

cd frontend
[ -d node_modules ] || bun install
bun x vite dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3002
```

## Kubernetes Port-Forward Development

Use local kubeconfig paths and background port-forwards only when the existing dev workflow requires live cluster services. Because port-forwarding usually needs functions, traps, PATH setup, and logs, put the logic in a wrapper script.

```toml
# THIS IS AUTOGENERATED. DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
version = 1
name = "cluster-backed-app"

[setup]
script = ""

[[actions]]
name = "运行"
icon = "run"
command = "/bin/bash /Users/me/projects/cluster-backed-app/.codex/environments/run-dev.sh"
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

LOG_FILE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cluster-backed-app-codex-run.log"
exec > >(tee -a "$LOG_FILE") 2>&1

export PATH="$HOME/Library/pnpm:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:$PATH"
: "${KUBECONFIG:?KUBECONFIG must come from the project's local environment configuration}"

for tool in pnpm kubectl lsof; do
  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    echo "missing required tool: $tool"
    echo "log file: $LOG_FILE"
    exit 127
  }
done

start_port_forward() {
  namespace="$1"
  service="$2"
  mapping="$3"
  local_port="${mapping%%:*}"

  if lsof -nP -iTCP:"$local_port" -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "local port $local_port already listening; reusing it"
    return 0
  fi

  kubectl -n "$namespace" port-forward "svc/$service" "$mapping" &
}

start_port_forward dev-services postgres 5432:5432
start_port_forward dev-services redis 6379:6379

cd /Users/me/projects/cluster-backed-app
pnpm dev
```

## Quoting Notes

- Prefer TOML literal strings `'''...'''` only for short multiline shell commands.
- For complex commands, keep TOML single-line and move the shell program into `.codex/environments/*.sh`.
- If the shell command itself uses single quotes, wrap it carefully and validate the TOML after editing.
- Prefer `cd "/absolute/path"` when paths contain spaces or the action may run from an unknown working directory.
- Keep the foreground dev server as the last command so the action does not exit immediately.
